about: Pokémon Kanto Squad's Trainer teams: roles, archetypes, rules and tiers for every Stadium mode (Ranked, Link, Friendly and any added later). Edit it with 'Pokemon Kanto Squad Team Config.html'; the game reads it when it's built (sh src/build.sh).

snow_veil_aurora_veil_offense.name: Snow · Aurora Veil setter (Aurora Veil offense)

electric_setter.name: Electric Terrain · setter (Electric Surge, Hadron Engine)

archetypes.name: Rain
archetypes.plan: Rain Dance starts rain for 5 rounds (8 with a Damp Rock): Water moves hit ×1.5 and Fire moves ×0.5, Swift Swim doubles Speed, and Thunder and Hurricane never miss. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone

subs.name: Swift Swim offense
subs.plan: This one's fast: the rain goes up and three or four sweepers take it from there

subs.name: Rain balance
subs.plan: This one's steadier: supports keep the team safe while three sweepers use the rain

archetypes.name: Sun
archetypes.plan: a Drought or Orichalcum Pulse Pokémon brings harsh sunlight as it comes in, for 5 rounds (8 with a Heat Rock): Fire moves hit ×1.5 and Water moves ×0.5, Chlorophyll gives Speed +2, Solar Beam and Solar Blade fire the same turn at ×1.5. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone

subs.name: Sun offense
subs.plan: Fire and Solar moves hit hard in the sun

subs.name: Chlorophyll offense
subs.plan: In the sun the Chlorophyll sweepers outspeed nearly everything

archetypes.name: Sand
archetypes.plan: a Sand Stream Pokémon whips up a sandstorm as it comes in, for 5 rounds (8 with a Smooth Rock): everything but Rock, Ground and Steel types loses 1/16 of its HP a turn, Rock, Ground and Steel types get Sp. Def +1, Sand Rush gives Speed +2 and Sand Force powers up Rock, Ground and Steel moves. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone

subs.name: Sand balance
subs.plan: The storm and entry hazards wear foes down while the sweepers finish them

subs.name: Sand offense
subs.plan: Sand Rush and Sand Force sweepers hit hard in the storm

archetypes.name: Snow
archetypes.plan: a Snow Warning Pokémon brings the snow as it comes in (hail and snow are one weather here), for 5 rounds (8 with an Icy Rock): everything but Ice types loses 1/16 of its HP a turn, Ice types get Defense +1, Blizzard never misses, Aurora Veil can go up. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone

subs.name: Aurora Veil offense
subs.plan: Aurora Veil cuts the damage the team takes while three or four sweepers go to work

subs.name: Blizzard spam
subs.plan: Blizzard never misses in the snow and hits every foe at once

archetypes.name: Trick Room
archetypes.plan: Trick Room flips the turn order for 5 rounds, so the slowest Pokémon move first and slow heavy hitters do the damage; the setter puts it up the moment it comes in, without using its turn, and its Room Service makes it last 8 rounds. The second setter waits on the bench until the room is down: coming in while it's up would end it

subs.name: Hard Trick Room
subs.plan: Everyone's slow, so the whole team wants the room up

subs.name: Semi-Room
subs.plan: Three slow sweepers for the room and supports to keep them safe

archetypes.name: Tailwind
archetypes.plan: Tailwind gives the whole team Speed +2 for 4 rounds and the Pokémon out there +10% turn meter at once, so the attackers get their turns first; the setter has priority (Prankster or a priority move, and the Quick Claw) so it gets the wind going before the other side moves

subs.name: Tailwind offense
subs.plan: All-out attack while the tailwind blows

subs.name: Tailwind balance
subs.plan: Tailwind plus a few Pokémon that hold up once it runs out

archetypes.name: Priority Offense
archetypes.plan: every priority move a Pokémon knows adds 10% turn meter for each point of priority the moment it comes in (Quick Attack +10%, Fake Out +30%, Protect +40%, Helping Hand +50%; a priority Ability and a Quick Claw too), and they stack, so the team moves first and its hardest hitters strike before the other side can act

subs.name: Nuke Spam
subs.plan: Priority gets them in first, then high-power single-target moves, with the items and Abilities that power them up

subs.name: Cleave Spam
subs.plan: Priority gets them in first, then spread moves hit every foe at once, with the items and Abilities that power them up

subs.name: Status Spam
subs.plan: Priority gets them in first to spread sleep, burns, paralysis and poison before the other side can act, and the hitters finish the job

subs.name: Dark Spam
subs.plan: Three Dark-type attackers get in first with priority and hit with Dark moves, Sucker Punch, Knock Off and the like, powered by Black Glasses and their Abilities

archetypes.name: Psychic Spam
archetypes.plan: a Psychic Surge Pokémon sets Psychic Terrain as it comes in, for 5 rounds (8 with a Terrain Extender): Psychic moves from Pokémon on the ground hit ×1.5, Expanding Force hits every foe at ×1.5, and priority moves can't touch the team's grounded Pokémon. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone

subs.name: Psychic Surge
subs.plan: The setter leads, and grounded Psychic attackers hit hard in the terrain

archetypes.name: Follow Me
archetypes.plan: the redirector comes in first and its Follow Me, Rage Powder or Spotlight goes off by itself the moment it's out, without using its turn, pulling the attacks away while its partners set up for free

subs.name: Physical Setup
subs.plan: Swords Dance, Shift Gear, Victory Dance, Dragon Dance or Belly Drum behind the redirector

subs.name: Special Setup
subs.plan: Quiver Dance, Geomancy, Nasty Plot or Tail Glow behind the redirector

subs.name: Mixed Setup
subs.plan: Physical and special setup together, with Shell Smash, No Retreat, Clangorous Soul or, in the sun, Growth to boost both

archetypes.name: Hazard Phazing
archetypes.plan: entry hazards go up, then Dragon Tail, Circle Throw, Roar and Whirlwind keep dragging the foes out: every one dragged in takes the hazards again, loses its stat boosts and starts with an empty turn meter, while bulky Pokémon and healing hold on

subs.name: Hazard phazing
subs.plan: Hazards and phazers, with healing to keep the walls going

subs.name: Bulky phazing
subs.plan: Hazards, phazers and the bulkiest Pokémon, which outlast everything they drag in

archetypes.name: Hyper Offense
archetypes.plan: hit hard and fast: screens or hazards from leads that move first, then setup sweepers boost and clean up before the other side gets going

subs.name: Dual Screens
subs.plan: The screen setters move first (Prankster or the Quick Claw) to get Reflect and Light Screen up, with Light Clay for 8 rounds, and the sweepers boost behind them

subs.name: Setup chain
subs.plan: A fast lead with the Quick Claw lays hazards first, then setup sweepers boost and clean up

subs.name: Priority rush
subs.plan: Three leads with priority attacks: each one adds turn meter by its priority the moment they're sent out (+10% for most, +20% for Extreme Speed), and they stack, so the team moves first and keeps hitting

archetypes.name: Bulky Offense
archetypes.plan: strong attackers that can take a hit too, so the team wins the trades

subs.name: Intimidate core
subs.plan: An Intimidate Pokémon lowers the foes' Attack as it comes in, and bulky attackers win the trades

subs.name: Bulky setup
subs.plan: Bulky Pokémon that boost while they take hits, behind an Intimidate

subs.name: Pledge core
subs.plan: The Kanto starters' Pledges: a teammate's different Pledge since your last turn makes yours a 150-power combined move, with a sea of fire, a swamp or a rainbow

archetypes.name: Balance
archetypes.plan: a bit of everything: an Intimidate, a bulky Pokémon with recovery, entry hazards, and strong attackers to win with

subs.name: Hazard balance
subs.plan: Entry hazards wear down every Pokémon that comes in

subs.name: Bulky balance
subs.plan: Bulky attackers and a wall with recovery outlast the trades

archetypes.name: Stall
archetypes.plan: screens, status, team healing and walls with recovery wear the other side down slowly with burns, poison and entry hazards

subs.name: Full stall
subs.plan: Everything is about outlasting: screens, status, team healing and walls

subs.name: Semi-stall
subs.plan: Screens, status and walls, plus a bulky Pokémon that boosts to finish things

subs.name: Trick Room stall
subs.plan: The setter puts Trick Room up as it comes in, so the slow walls move first and keep their health up while status and hazards do the damage

archetypes.name: Electric Terrain
archetypes.plan: an Electric Surge or Hadron Engine Pokémon sets Electric Terrain as it comes in, for 5 rounds (8 with a Terrain Extender): Electric moves from Pokémon on the ground hit ×1.5, nobody on the ground can fall asleep, and Quark Drive, Surge Surfer and an Electric Seed's holder get going. A second, harder-hitting setter waits on the bench to bring it back once it's gone, and one of the team always holds a Ring Target, so its Electric attacks still hit Ground types

subs.name: Electric Surge
subs.plan: The setter leads, three sweepers hit hard in the terrain, and the harder-hitting backup waits on the bench
